label: Period from the Coefficient
subgoals: For y = sin(bx), the period is 360/b degrees, or 2 pi/b radians.
For y = cos(bx), the same rule applies.
The period is always positive, so use the absolute value of b.

label: Frequency
subgoals: Frequency is the number of cycles in one unit of the horizontal variable.
A period of 180 degrees corresponds to two cycles in 360 degrees, so the frequency is two per full turn.
In applications, frequency is often measured in hertz, which counts cycles per second.

label: Comparing Graphs
subgoals: Two sine graphs with different b values have different periods but the same shape and amplitude.
The graph with the larger coefficient completes more cycles in the same window.
A phase shift changes where a cycle starts but not how long it lasts.
